# Sirach Chapter 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_013_page_001.jpg

---

**13:1** Whoever touches pitch will be defiled, and whoever associates with an arrogant person will become like him.

**13:2** Do not take up a burden beyond your strength, and do not associate with someone mightier and wealthier than yourself. What does a clay pot have in common with an iron kettle? The kettle strikes and the pot shatters.

**13:3** A rich man does wrong and even adds threats; a poor man is wronged and even must beg forgiveness.

**13:4** If you can be of use to him, he will exploit you; but if you have nothing to offer, he will abandon you.

**13:5** As long as you have something, he will stay with you; he will drain you dry and not feel sorry.

**13:6** Does he need you? He will deceive you; he will smile at you and raise your hopes; he will speak pleasantly to you and ask, "What do you need?"

**13:7** He will shame you at his feasts until he has stripped you bare — this more than once or twice; and in the end he will mock you. Afterward, when he sees you, he will pass you by and shake his head at you.

**13:8** Take heed not to be misled, and not to be humiliated in your eagerness for his company.

**13:9** When an important man invites you, hold back — and he will invite you all the more.

**13:10** Do not push forward lest you be thrust back; do not stay too far away lest you be forgotten.

**13:11** Do not presume to speak as his equal, and do not trust his many words; for with much talking he will test you, and with a smile he will probe you.

**13:12** One who shows no mercy is one who does not guard his words; he will not spare you from pain or chains.

**13:13** Be on guard and be very careful, for you are walking with your own downfall. When you hear these things, wake up even in your sleep.

**13:14** Love the Lord all your life, and call upon him for your salvation.

**13:15** Every creature loves its own kind, and every person his neighbor.

**13:16** All flesh associates with its own kind, and a person keeps company with those like himself.

**13:17** What fellowship does a wolf have with a lamb? No more does a sinner have with a righteous person.

**13:18** What peace is there between a hyena and a dog? And what peace between a rich man and a poor man?

**13:19** Wild donkeys in the desert are the prey of lions; so too, the poor are the feeding ground of the rich.

**13:20** Humility is an abomination to the proud; likewise, a poor man is an abomination to the rich.

**13:21** When a rich man stumbles, he is supported by friends; but when a poor man falls, even friends push him away.

**13:22** When a rich man slips, many rush to help; he says something improper and they find excuses for him. When a poor man slips, they rebuke him further; he speaks wisely and no one takes notice.

**13:23** The rich man speaks and everyone falls silent, and they praise his words to the sky; the poor man speaks and they ask, "Who is this?" — and if he stumbles, they push him down further still.

**13:24** Wealth is good where there is no sin attached to it; poverty is evil in the reckoning of the ungodly.

**13:25** A man's heart changes his face, whether for good or for evil.

**13:26** A glad face is the sign of a glad heart; but the search for wise words is wearisome labor.
